data.turoyo: <...> Nošo mənayxu d roməš d soyəm ḥarake gəd mṭaqṭaqno u babo. <...>
data.translation: <...> Anyone of you who stirs, who makes a move, I shall smash his father. <...>

rationale: Only attestation for restricted figurative I.2 and first Infectum box; conditional threat and direct personal object distinguish it from door-knocking.

summary: New sense 2: fig. (in einer Drohung) jemanden verprügeln
rationale: The conditional prohibition selects u babo as a direct personal object, unlike b-/ʕal-marked doors in I.1. The clause threatens violent pounding, not door-knocking. One attestation only; no unrestricted beating paradigm or actual assault is inferred.

data.turoyo: Aṯi u dawlatli lu bayto, mṭaqṭaqle bu tarʕo, omər: “Ftaḥ.” Ftəḥla u tarʕo.
data.translation: lief nach Hause und klopfte an der Thüre, indem er rief: »Mach auf!« Sie öffnete dieselbe;

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: second compact door-knocking episode.

data.turoyo: Azza i pire lu tarʕo d bə qoḏ̣e, mṭaqṭaqla ʕal u tarʕo, ftiḥalla u tarʕo, əmmi: "L ayko?"
data.translation: Die Alte ging an die Türe des Richters und klopfte an; man öffnete ihr und fragte sie: "Wohin?"

rationale: Thin Preterit and government variant: feminine agent, ʕal-marked door beside existing b-marked target.

summary: The inherited quadriliteral is filed as stem I; this assignment preserves that designation rather than silently changing it to Q. The clear forms are mṭaqṭaqle and feminine mṭaqṭaqla.
The knocked surface is b-marked in the existing and PrS 11 examples and ʕal-marked in PrS 78/5. This alternation does not establish separate senses.
57/201 suggests hammering on sheet metal, a possible participant extension of pochen. Its contracted form is insufficiently secure to add as a new spelling or metalworking sense.
Knocking at a door is compositional here; no idiom is added. The inherited unknown etymology remains unknown.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce round 2. All supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation; analyses and sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Quoted English is copied verbatim and labelled as machine translation. Round-1 proposals are the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.
R1 retains the quadriradical under the glossary's I label and only adds Preterit contexts. Jan mṭaqṭaqno with gəd independently supplies Infectum first-person morphology; initial m is lexical here.

Nošo mənayxu d roməš d soyəm ḥarake introduces a conditional threat; u babo is its direct object. This establishes a threatening personal-object use beyond knocking on a door, without claiming that any father was actually struck.
The new I.2 is restricted to the figurative threat evidence. It does not retroactively settle R1's uncertain sheet-metal form mtaqtole or prove an unrestricted literal beat sense.

A read-only mṭaqṭ search checks the existing verb contexts before treating the father phrase as a possible collocation. The one conditional threat does not independently establish a fixed idiom, so the lexical change is recorded once as the restricted sense rather than duplicated under Idiomatic phrases.

Is mṭaqṭaqno u babo a conventional abusive father formula, a figurative threat against the addressed person, or a literal threat against his father? Confirm the exact force before extending I.2 beyond this one context.
Does the threat imply repeated beating, a single heavy blow or broader ruin? The machine translation's smash is preserved only as supplied English, not treated as proof of a precise injury outcome.
